euronews.description: UK civil liberties campaign group Big Brother Watch has criticised the use of technologies such as drones and facial recognition.

euronews.title: Portugal's World Cup victory sparks celebrations in Lisbon
euronews.description: Thousands of fans in Lisbon celebrated Portugal's 5-0 World Cup victory over Uzbekistan, with Cristiano Ronaldo scoring twice and becoming the first player to score in six different World Cup tournaments.

euronews.title: Paris's Cirque d'Hiver begins renovation to restore its original splendour
euronews.description: Twenty ornamental frescoes from the Second Empire are to be restored over twelve to eighteen months. The seating, the polychrome ceiling canvas and the stained-glass windows will also be refurbished.

euronews.description: Iceland resumes commercial whaling after a two-year pause, with two fin whales processed at the Hvalur facility, reigniting controversy and protests.

euronews.description: The NPA has more than 450 staff based in Ukraine, where it has been carrying out mine clearance activities since 2023.

euronews.title: Heat records tumble: Spain breaks two June records
euronews.description: Spain's state meteorological agency, Aemet, reported that Monday and Tuesday were the hottest June days on record in mainland Spain since at least 1950.

euronews.title: Madrid, Woody Allen's new cinematic muse
euronews.description: Woody Allen’s next film, set entirely in Madrid, will treat the city as a star. Filming begins in October, following in the footsteps of New York, Paris, Rome and Barcelona.

euronews.title: EU proposes tax overhaul to cut business costs by €8 billion a year
euronews.description: The reform would reduce the compliance burden for businesses and facilitate cross-border payments.

euronews.title: European heatwave forces Eiffel Tower early closure and tourist attraction shutdowns
euronews.description: From the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre to Buckingham Palace's Changing of the Guard, soaring temperatures are forcing attractions to close, shorten opening hours and cancel events as a heatwave grips Europe.

euronews.title: EU diplomatic service announces new top posts with strong defence focus
euronews.description: The EEAS has named Kajsa Ollongren as secretary general, with Matti Maasikas and David Cvach in deputy roles. The defence-focused appointments come as the bloc's foreign policy machinery faces increasing pressure.

euronews.title: Tehran labels framework deal 'US defeat' as Trump threatens to halt talks
euronews.description: Iranian key negotiator hailed the US–Iran framework deal as a “declaration of US defeat,” while Trump warned that talks would end immediately if reports that Tehran is seeking to impose tolls on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz prove to be true.

euronews.title: EU scales back Ukraine's accession timetable due to Hungarian resistance
euronews.description: Faced with renewed resistance from Hungary, the EU has been forced to change plans and now aims to unblock two, rather than five, accession clusters with Ukraine and Moldova before the summer break.

euronews.title: Senior UK minister rules out leadership challenge as Burnham edges closer to Downing Street
euronews.description: Jones' decision removes a major obstacle standing between Burnham and the UK's top job and could mean the latter is in Downing Street as early as July.

euronews.title: Brent crude falls below $74 for first time since start of the Iran war
euronews.description: Brent crude dropped below $74 a barrel on Wednesday for the first time since the start of the Iran war in late February, as investors continued to price out the geopolitical risk premium that had driven energy markets higher during the conflict.

euronews.title: 'It will be easy to employ me' - Portugal pushes vocational training to fill skills gap
euronews.description: Portugal is pushing vocational training, backed by nearly €1.5bn in EU funding, to prepare 55% of its secondary school students for in-demand jobs.

euronews.title: Pearls of the Tian Shan: Exploring the natural wonders of Kolsai Lakes National Park
euronews.description: Kolsai Lakes National Park ranks among Kazakhstan’s top ecotourism destinations, attracting visitors with its pristine lakes, alpine landscapes and well-preserved ecosystems.

euronews.title: Grand Voyager | Exploring Nairobi
euronews.description: From roaming wildlife to luxury hidden retreats, Nairobi is a destination on every traveller's bucket list. But what is it about Kenya that makes it so unique?

rfi.title: US releases experimental Ebola drug for DR Congo outbreak trials
rfi.description: Experimental Ebola drugs are being shipped to Democratic Republic of Congo as the United States releases doses of a treatment for clinical trials in a widening outbreak that has caused more than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths, the World Health Organization and US officials have said.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: 'The average British citizen has lost over £3,000 a year'
rfi.description: Ten years after the UK voted to leave the European Union, Brexit remains deeply divisive, with supporters and critics still at odds over its political and economic legacy. As part of RFI’s series marking the 10th anniversary of the referendum, we spoke to politics and international relations professor John Barry, one of its staunchest opponents.

rfi.title: Seven European countries urge ‘immediate halt’ to Sudan violence
rfi.description: Seven European countries have called on Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to immediately stop their assault on El-Obeid, a city in Sudan's North Kordofan state, warning of credible signs that a major offensive could be imminent as civilians face worsening shortages of food, water and fuel.

rfi.title: France scrambles to respond, as June heatwave grips Europe
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to hold a crisis meeting on Tuesday, after Météo France reported that the country's average temperature had broken a June record. Elsewhere in Europe, several countries are also struggling with the heatwave, which has led to a number of deaths and disruption to public services.

rfi.title: Portugal delays handover of French mother accused of abandoning children
rfi.description: Portuguese authorities have refused to immediately extradite to France a 41-year-old woman suspected of abandoning her two young children, who were found last month crying at the side of a road south of Lisbon.

rfi.title: Ghana dig in for stalemate with England at World Cup
rfi.description: Ghana fought their way to a 0-0 draw with England on Tuesday night that took them closer to qualifying for the knockout stages at the World Cup for the first time since their dazzling run to the last eight in 2010 in South Africa.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch was inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday in a sombre ceremony, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the country’s most symbolic events.

rfi.title: French government begins disciplinary action over child abuse case failings
rfi.description: The French government has announced disciplinary action against a magistrate and two gendarmerie officers over the handling of a suspect in child abuse case, which has lead to public outcry. This comes on the heels of a report which pointed to serious failings of the justice system, particularly with regards to minors.

rfi.title: Kenya halts US Ebola facility, health minister apologises for disobeying orders
rfi.description: Kenya has ordered a halt to preparations for a controversial US-run Ebola quarantine facility, the health minister told a court Tuesday, after being held in contempt for ignoring a previous stop-work order. The project has prompted widespread anger, and several people were killed during protests earlier this month.

rfi.title: EU gambles on Taliban talks to fast-track Afghan deportations
rfi.description: A Taliban delegation is due to fly into Brussels on Tuesday, having been granted a one-day visa to hold talks with the EU on returning failed asylum seekers to Afghanistan. However, human rights groups have warned that the scheme runs counter to the bloc's values.

rfi.title: Mbappé's double on 100th appearance fires France into World Cup knockout stages
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé marked his 100th cap for France on Monday night with two goals in their 3-0 win over Iraq in a game that took more than four hours to complete due to thunder storms over Philadelphia.

rfi.title: Messi notches up World Cup goals record to take Argentina into knockout stages
rfi.description: Argentina skipper Lionel Messi added another accolade to his otherworldly list of achievements on Monday when he became the record goalscorer at World Cups since the inception of the tournament in 1930

rfi.title: Haaland scores twice as Norway outwit Senegal to reach last 32 at World Cup
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice on Monday night as Norway advanced to the knockout stages at the World Cup following a pulsating 3-2 victory over Senegal in New Jersey.

rfi.title: Repeated errors in handling of rape case linked to French girl's death: report
rfi.description: An administrative investigation ordered after the death of 11 year-old Lyhanna in southern France has revealed serious failings in how a previous rape complaint against the main suspect was handled. The case has brought the French judicial and police system under stark scrutiny, especially regarding cases of child abuse.

rfi.title: 'Poison in your coffee' report sounds alarm over widespread pesticide use
rfi.description: Coffee production around the world depends heavily on pesticides, leaving millions of farm workers exposed to harmful chemicals while pesticide residues are also found in exported coffee beans, a report published on Monday warned.

rfi.title: Paris court rejects bid to reopen probe into Caribbean chlordecone contamination
rfi.description: The Paris appeals court has upheld a decision not to reopen a criminal investigation into the use of chlordecone, a toxic pesticide that has been linked to cancer and other health problems in around 90 percent of the adult population in Guadeloupe and Martinique.

rfi.title: UN warns of an 'imminent risk of mass atrocities' in Sudan's Kordofan
rfi.description: In Sudan, NGOs and the UN have warned of an "imminent risk of mass atrocities" in El-Obeid, a major city in North Kordofan. This comes as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) step up their campaign against the regular army in the region.

rfi.title: France, Germany reach deal on arms maker KNDS, opening door to stock market
rfi.description: France and Germany announced Monday a deal for the joint governance of Amsterdam-headquartered arms maker KNDS, paving the way for a blockbuster share offering as they seek to boost faltering European defence cooperation.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, canicule : après le pic de mercredi, les fortes chaleurs se poursuivront jusqu’à ce week-end sur une grande partie de la France, 40 °C  à 42 °C prévus
lemonde.description: Deux départements, la Haute-Garonne et les Deux-Sèvres, basculent « pour la première fois de la saison » sur un « niveau de danger très élevé » pour les feux de forêts, a annoncé mercredi Météo-France.

lemonde.title: « La menace de la force était bien plus dissuasive que l’étalage de cette dernière par Donald Trump dans la guerre contre l’Iran »
lemonde.description: La stratégie de sécurité nationale du président des Etats-Unis, publiée en décembre 2025, a été lourdement mise à mal ces six derniers mois, observe dans sa chronique Gilles Paris, éditorialiste au « Monde ».

lemonde.title: Entre le Luxembourg et Dubaï, les millions cachés de Fabrice Andjoua, fils de l’ancien président gabonais
lemonde.description: Le fils d’Omar Bongo a dissimulé à l’étranger un patrimoine de plusieurs millions d’euros, entre voiture de luxe et biens immobiliers à Dubaï, d’après l’enquête « OpenLux » coordonnée notamment par « Le Monde ». Le décalage avec ses revenus de haut fonctionnaire gabonais interroge sur de potentiels « biens mal acquis ».

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la Russie affirme qu’il n’existe « aucun accord » pour la reprise de négociations de paix avec Kiev
lemonde.description: Dmitri Peskov a réaffirmé qu’il s’agissait de la « position constante » de Vladimir Poutine. « Il le répète en permanence. Il l’a dit il y a deux ans au ministère des affaires étrangères, où il a tracé les grands axes de notre position, nécessaires pour mettre fin à la guerre », a ajouté le représentant de la présidence russe.

lemonde.title: Planning familial : en Gironde, la subvention de l’agence régionale de santé finalement maintenue pour 2026
lemonde.description: L’ARS, qui avait annoncé, mercredi 17 juin, la suspension de la subvention de 160 000 euros octroyée chaque année à l’association, la lui versera cette année, pour la dernière fois. Elle s’engage toutefois à l’accompagner pour trouver des partenaires, afin de prendre le relais et éviter sa fermeture.

lemonde.title: Cyberpédocriminalité : une trentaine de consommateurs d’images de violences sexuelles sur mineurs interpellés sur tout le territoire
lemonde.description: Lundi 22, mardi 23 et mercredi 24 juin, une centaine de policiers et de gendarmes ont ciblé des consommateurs de vidéos particulièrement violentes, des hommes de « toutes les catégories sociales ».

lemonde.title: « Les politiques migratoires européennes ignorent les besoins spécifiques des femmes et des personnes LGBT+ »
lemonde.description: Dans une tribune au « Monde », les représentants d’Osez le féminisme !, de SOS Racisme et de l’Institut du genre en géopolitique déplorent que la prise en compte des violences spécifiques auxquelles sont exposées les femmes et personnes LGBT+ demeure largement absente de la mise en œuvre du pacte sur la migration et l’asile de l’UE.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : les opposants à Marine Tondelier obtiennent la tenue d’un conseil fédéral extraordinaire au sein des Ecologistes le 30 juin
lemonde.description: Les opposants en interne cherchent à remettre en cause la consultation des militants au sujet de la présidentielle prévue au début de juillet. Ils critiquent la formulation de ce qui sera soumis au vote.

lemonde.title: Israël : une commission de l’ONU dénonce la poursuite d’un « génocide » dans la bande de Gaza
lemonde.description: Dans un rapport publié le 23 juin, la commission dénonce de nouveau un « génocide » en cours dans l’enclave palestinienne. Israël a qualifié ce rapport de « diffamatoire ».

lemonde.title: IA : « Pékin gère désormais son immense écosystème d’innovation à la manière d’une grande plateforme numérique »
lemonde.description: Face à la course mondiale pour la souveraineté technologique, les Etats-Unis semblent négliger les nouvelles stratégies déployées par la Chine, explique, dans sa chronique, la professeure de droit américaine Angela Huyue Zhang.

lemonde.title: « Charli XCX. Alone Together », sur Arte.tv : la naissance d’un album en pleine période de confinement
lemonde.description: Bradley Bell et Pablo Jones-Soler dévoilent le processus créatif de la chanteuse pop britannique, entre interrogations et réussites, pour les 11 titres de « How I’m Feeling Now », écrits durant la pandémie de Covid-19.

lemonde.title: La fréquentation des théâtres progresse, portée par un public vieillissant et favorisé
lemonde.description: Selon le baromètre 2026 « Les Français et le théâtre » réalisé par Médiamétrie, 13 millions de spectateurs sont allés au théâtre, mais le nombre de pièces vues en moyenne sur douze mois a diminué.

lemonde.description: Il s’agit du premier cas jamais diagnostiqué sur le territoire français. La situation est suivie « de très près » par le premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, selon son entourage, cité par l’Agence France-Presse.

zeit.description: Wenn der Direktor zum Unterrichtsbesuch kommt, soll das Können der Pädagogen geprüft werden. Und es beginnt ein absurdes Theaterspiel. Die Lehrerkolumne

zeit.title: Hitzewelle: Temperaturen in Spanien steigen auf neuen Juni-Rekordwert
zeit.description: Seit Beginn der Aufzeichnungen war der Juni in Spanien nicht so heiß wie in diesen Tagen. In Frankreich wurde der Bahnverkehr wegen der Hitze eingeschränkt. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Bahn-Störung: Wie ein Fehler die ganze Bahn lahmlegen konnte
zeit.description: Eine Störung hat den Zugverkehr in Deutschland zeitweise lahmgelegt. Wie lassen sich solche Ausfälle künftig verhindern? Und: Ermittlungen nach Messerattacke in Göttingen

france24fr.title: Soudan : El-Obeid au bord de la catastrophe humanitaire selon l'ONU
france24fr.description: Au Soudan, une nouvelle crise humanitaire se dessine à El-Obeid. Cette ville dans la région du Kordofan est assiégée depuis plusieurs mois par les militaires du FSR. Sans livraison en eau ni en nourriture, El-Obeid est au bord de la catastrophe humanitaire. La communauté internationale appelle à la fin des violences.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Présidentielle en Colombie : le candidat de gauche reconnaît la victoire d'Abelardo de la Espriella
Présidentielle en Colombie : le candidat de gauche reconnaît la victoire d'Abelardo de la Espriella
france24fr.description: Trois jours après le second tour d'élection présidentielle le plus serré de l'histoire du pays, et alors qu'il en rejetait initialement les résultats, le candidat de gauche, Iván Cepeda, a finalement reconnu mercredi la victoire de celui de l'ultradroite, Abelardo de la Espriella.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : Ebola gagne du terrain dans les mines d’or de Mongbwalu
france24fr.description: L’épidémie d’Ebola continue de s’étendre en République démocratique du Congo, avec plus de 250 morts selon le dernier bilan officiel. À Mongbwalu, l’un des principaux foyers de contamination, les mineurs poursuivent leur activité faute d’alternative économique, malgré la peur de la maladie et les difficultés croissantes pour contenir le virus.

france24fr.title: Ebola : premier cas confirmé en France
france24fr.description: La France a confirmé son premier cas d’Ebola lié à l’épidémie en cours en RDC : un médecin de retour d’une mission humanitaire a été placé à l’isolement, tandis que les autorités ont lancé le traçage de ses contacts et assurent que le risque pour la population reste très faible.

france24fr.title: Cinéma : le général de Gaulle revient encore plus fort
france24fr.description: Dans ce nouveau numéro de "À l'Affiche 100 % cinéma", Natacha Vesnitch et Thomas Baurez évoquent l'actualité dans les salles cette semaine. Ils débutent avec le second volet du diptyque sur le général de Gaulle signé Antonin Baudry. Après "L'âge de fer", voici "J'écris ton nom", qui suit les dernières heures de la Seconde Guerre mondiale en France. Simon Abkarian reprend du service dans la peau du grand homme. Thomas Baurez souligne la qualité de cet opus dont la sortie a été avancée pour coller

france24fr.title: 🔴 Canicule : les trois quarts de la France placés en alerte maximale jeudi
Mondial 2026 : deuxième défaite consécutive pour le Sénégal
france24fr.description: La nuit a été difficile pour les supporters sénégalais, après la défaite du Sénégal face à la Norvège (3-2). Les Lions de la Teranga concèdent ainsi un deuxième revers consécutif dans ce début de Coupe du monde, et compliquent sérieusement leurs chances de qualification pour le deuxième tour.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : les prix des maillots des Léopards s'envolent pendant le Mondial
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, l’engouement autour de la sélection nationale atteint des sommets. Mais dans l’est du pays, cette ferveur se confronte à une autre réalité : le prix des maillots des Léopards s’envole notamment à cause de la fermeture de la frontière avec le Rwanda. À Bukavu, la passion pour l’équipe nationale se heurte ainsi à la hausse des coûts, qui rend ces équipements de plus en plus difficiles à se procurer.

france24fr.title: Australie : le fléau des lapins, espèce devenue invasive
france24fr.description: En France, on les considère comme inoffensifs. Mais en Australie, les lapins sont une catastrophe pour l'économie et l'environnement. Introduits par des colons britanniques au milieu du XIXe siècle – qui voulaient s'adonner à la chasse sur le temps libre – les lapins, en l'absence de prédateur naturel sur l'île-continent, se sont très rapidement multipliés et couvert la quasi-totalité du territoire.

france24fr.title: En Grèce, les secteurs du tourisme, de l'alimentation et du BTP en grève pour de meilleurs salaires
france24fr.description: Une grève massive des travailleurs du tourisme, de l'alimentation et de la construction a lieu mercredi en Grèce, les professionnels de ces secteurs exigeant des augmentations de salaires et de meilleures conditions de travail. "Le travail s'intensifie et les salaires ne suivent pas", déplorent-ils, alors que de nombreux jeunes Grecs envisagent de partir à l'étranger où les salaires sont plus élevés.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : en Ituri, plus d’un mois après le début d’Ebola, "c'est une épidémie qui va durer"
france24fr.description: Alors qu'un premier cas vient d'être enregistré sur le sol français, à Mongbwalu, épicentre de l’épidémie d’Ebola à l’est de la RD Congo, des premiers cas de guérison ont été recensés. Mais si la riposte à l’épidémie s’organise, les professionnels de santé restent inquiets face à la progression continue du nombre de cas.

france24fr.title: "J'essaie de tenir, jour après jour" : ces travailleurs en première ligne face à la canicule
france24fr.description: Sous une chaleur écrasante et des températures records, la France tourne au ralenti. Au milieu des rues désertées et des terrasses abandonnées de Paris, des milliers de travailleurs continuent d’assurer leur mission en plein soleil. Ouvriers, livreurs, agents municipaux... Reportage auprès de ceux qui affrontent la canicule sans pouvoir se mettre à l’abri.

france24fr.title: Didier Deschamps s’absente du Mondial pour assister aux obsèques de sa mère
france24fr.description: L'entraîneur français Didier Deschamps ne sera pas sur le banc des Bleus face à la Norvège vendredi, après avoir appris le décès de sa mère. Il a quitté le camp de base de l’équipe de France et rentre en France pour quelques jours afin d’assister aux obsèques, laissant son adjoint Guy Stéphan assurer l’intérim.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Cristiano Ronaldo rugit encore
france24fr.description: Critiqué après une première ratée face à la RD Congo, Cristiano Ronaldo a répondu par un doublé mardi contre l'Ouzbékistan, balayé (5-0) par le Portugal, désormais tout près des 16es de finale. La RD Congo, battue par la Colombie (1-0), jouera sa qualification pour la phase à élimination directe face à l'Ouzbekistan.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Ronaldo brille, l’Angleterre cale, la Croatie assure l’essentiel
france24fr.description: Lors de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes, Cristiano Ronaldo a signé un doublé et porté le Portugal vers une large victoire 5-0 face à l’Ouzbékistan, confirmant son record de but dans six Coupes du monde. De son côté, l’Angleterre a été tenue en échec par le Ghana (0-0), tandis que la Croatie s’est imposée de justesse face au Panama (1-0) sans encore valider sa qualification pour les huitièmes.

france24fr.title: Espagne : Pedro Sánchez face à une vague d’affaires de corruption dans son entourage
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sánchez a démenti toute « corruption généralisée » autour de son gouvernement, alors que plusieurs affaires touchent de près son entourage politique et familial. Parmi les personnes mises en cause figurent notamment son épouse, son frère, ainsi que d’anciens proches comme l’ex-ministre des Transports condamné et l’ancien Premier ministre José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, tandis que l’opposition réclame sa démission.

france24fr.title: Soudan : à El Obeid, la catastrophe humanitaire est proche
france24fr.description: À El Obeid, au Soudan, la situation se dégrade rapidement et rappelle les violences survenues à El Fasher en novembre 2025, où des milliers, voire des dizaines de milliers de personnes auraient été tuées. La ville est désormais encerclée par les Forces de soutien rapides (FSR), qui multiplient les bombardements aveugles, rendant la vie des civils de plus en plus insupportable. Face à cette escalade, la communauté internationale appelle à un arrêt immédiat des combats. Les précisions de Bastien R

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Visp bricht seinen eigenen Juni-Rekord mit 36,8 Grad +++ Die Bahn in Frankreich stellt den Verkehr teilweise ein
nzz.description: Wo ist es gerade besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf Mensch und Umwelt? Hier finden Sie die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren und Bränden in Europa.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Schiffe passieren laut der Uno die Meerenge über zwei Routen +++ Der US-Senat stimmt gegen Trumps eigenmächtige Kriegsführung
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: Linker, jünger, antiisraelisch: Mamdanis Sozialisten besiegen das demokratische Establishment in New Yorker Vorwahlen
nzz.description: New Yorks sozialistischer Bürgermeister Mamdani setzt seinen Siegeszug auch auf nationaler Ebene fort: Bei den Vorwahlen zum Kongress gewannen drei seiner Kandidaten. Es ist eine Blamage für die Parteiführung der Demokraten und ein Warnsignal für Israel.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Bahnchaos in Deutschland: Die Deutsche Bahn hat beim Schutz ihrer Infrastruktur geschlampt
nzz.description: Die nächtliche Störung ist mehr als bloss eine Panne unter vielen. Sie offenbart ein zentrales Problem beim Bemühen um mehr Resilienz für die zentralen Funktionen eines Landes.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Deutschland: Ermittlungen gegen Mutter nach Fund von Babyleiche +++ Razzien wegen Verdacht auf Sabotageakt gegen Gasversorgung
«Nicht die Schweizer Mentalität»: Die UBS-Vorschläge zur Reform der Altersvorsorge sorgen für Kritik
nzz.description: Die Ökonomen der Grossbank raten, das Dreisäulensystem komplett zu überarbeiten. Branchenexperten gehen die Ideen zu weit.

nzz.title: Den Menschen in Myanmar droht das Vergessen
nzz.description: Die Uno weist darauf hin, dass die humanitäre Hilfe in dem Land zusammenbricht. Aber Unterstützung zu leisten, ist für Hilfsorganisationen kompliziert. Das Risiko ist gross, dass die Gelder am Ende in die Taschen der Generäle wandern oder zu den bewaffneten Rebellen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Der Bund hat wieder mehr Geld. Der Überschuss soll in die Armee fliessen – die Pressekonferenz zum Nachlesen
nzz.description: Die Mehrwertsteuer soll für die Landesverteidigung erhöht werden, aber weniger stark als geplant: So hat es der Bundesrat am Mittwoch beschlossen. Volk und Stände haben das letzte Wort.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Keine Spielchen mit der Schuldenbremse – auch nicht für die Armee
nzz.description: Der Bundesrat will weiterhin die Steuern erhöhen, um die Nachrüstung zu finanzieren. Das ist zwar bitter, aber immer noch viel besser, als die Schuldenbremse auszuhebeln. Mittlerweile will sogar die FDP tricksen. Das ist beunruhigend.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Günther Dissertori wird neuer ETH-Zürich-Präsident +++ Der Bundesrat will das Jagdgesetz anpassen
«Kein Schwimmen, nur schauen!»: Wie Migranten mit Gefahren am Wasser vertraut gemacht werden
nzz.description: Junge Männer aus dem Ausland laufen besonders Gefahr, zu ertrinken. Gezielte Präventionsmassnahmen sollen helfen – zum Beispiel ein Spaziergang an der Limmat in Zürich.

nzz.title: 100 Stellen weg, 113 Millionen Franken gespart: Der Bundesrat stellt seine Entwicklungshilfe neu auf
nzz.description: Der Bund will sich mehr in Krisengebieten engagieren – auch auf Kosten von langfristigen internationalen Projekten. Er zieht sich beispielsweise aus Lateinamerika zurück.

nzz.title: Milliardengeschenk für Iran: Die USA heben die Ölsanktionen fast ganz auf und bescheren Teheran neue Einnahmen
nzz.description: Um die Friedensgespräche zu erleichtern, darf iranisches Erdöl nahezu überall verkauft werden – sogar in die USA. Washington zeigt das grösste Entgegenkommen seit der Islamischen Revolution von 1979.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ebola-Ausbruch in Zentralafrika: Erster Fall in Frankreich nachgewiesen
nzz.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation WHO hat den Gesundheitsnotstand ausgerufen. Es werden weitere Infizierte erwartet. Die wichtigsten Antworten zum Ebolavirus.

nzz.title: «Niemand kann sagen, wie lange das noch gut geht»: Die KI-Skepsis kehrt an die Finanzmärkte zurück
nzz.description: Am Dienstag haben die Aktienkurse von Technologieunternehmen in Asien und den USA stark verloren. Anleger müssen sich darauf einstellen, dass es volatil weitergeht.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Polizei-News aus Zürich: Mehrere Schüsse bei Streit in Bülach gefallen, die Polizei fahndet nach den Tätern
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

observador.title: "Já foi desafetado há anos": ministra sobre Cinema Paris
observador.description: “Já foi desafetado há anos”, diz Margarida Balseiro Lopes, recusando comentar críticas da Academia Portuguesa de Cinema à demolição aprovada pela Câmara de Lisboa. Cinema está fechado desde 1985.

observador.title: "Memorando prova o fracasso da administração de Trump"
observador.description: Luís Tomé afirma que o acordo de paz é favorável ao Irão. O professor e investigador defende ainda que Israel foi ignorado no acordo e pode tentar boicotar a paz.

observador.title: Mulher mantida em cativeiro 12 anos pelo marido no Paquistão
observador.description: Sylvie Yasmina e os cinco filhos foram encontrados num quarto degradado, com hematomas. Um dos filhos fugiu para apresentar queixa à polícia. A família planeia regressar à França.

observador.title: Shakira usou sósia na cerimónia de abertura do Mundial?
observador.description: Na atuação da abertura do Mundial de 2026 da canção Dai Dai, vários internautas levantaram a suspeita de que Shakira teria usado uma sósia durante a performance. Será mesmo assim?

observador.title: Preços da habitação abrandam
observador.description: Os preços da habitação desaceleraram pela primeira vez em quase dois anos, segundo dados do INE. Ainda assim, cresceram 17,8% no primeiro trimestre.

observador.title: EUA começam a suavizar restrições do Irão no Mundial
observador.description: Ao contrário do que aconteceu nos dois primeiros jogos, iranianos vão poder entrar nos EUA dois dias antes da última jornada da fase de grupos. Treinador já tinha antecipado hipótese durante a semana.

observador.title: Eutanásia administrada a menor de 12 anos nos Países Baixos
observador.description: A operação foi efetuada em 2025, segundo o relatório divulgado pela ministra da Saúde, Sophie Hermans, na segunda-feira. O médico que eutanasiou está a ser investigado pelo Ministério Pública.

observador.title: Tráfego no estreito de Ormuz sobe para 31 navios por dia
observador.description: O número contrasta com a média diária de 100 a 120 navios que passavam por esta passagem marítima antes do início do conflito armado, iniciado a 28 de fevereiro, pela ofensiva dos EUA e Israel.

observador.title: Vídeo mostra ataque do Irão a Israel na última ofensiva?
observador.description: Mísseis e a resposta da defesa aérea. Vídeo partilhado nas redes sociais mostraria impactos em Israel da última vaga de ataques iranianos que ocorreram em junho de 2026. Será mesmo assim?

observador.title: Presidente da República quer lei do mecenato "mais atrativa"
observador.description: António José Seguro pediu uma lei do mecenato "mais atrativa", para incentivar a cooperação entre público e privado no apoio à cultura, num discurso na abertura do festival literário Babell, no Porto.

observador.title: BdP quer evitar tolerância ao branqueamento de capitais
observador.description: João Raposo, do Banco de Portugal, foi ouvido no parlamento sobre o aumento de comunicações de operações suspeitas ao DCIAP. Fraude digital e melhores controlos internos explicam a subida.

observador.title: EASA manda inspecionar 16 aviões A380 com fissuras nas asas
observador.description: Agência Europeia para a Segurança da Aviação identificou falhas na longarina central da asa em 15 aviões da Emirates e um da Qantas. Problemas semelhantes com este modelo já tinham ocorrido em 2012.

observador.title: Candidatos apoiados por Mamdani vencem primárias
observador.description: Candidatos progressistas venceram três distritos, derrotando políticos experientes. "Não foi o fim de um movimento político [...) Foi o começo", diz o presidente da Câmara de Nova Iorque.

observador.title: As notícias das 16h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: CDS propõe duplicar dedução em IRS para famílias numerosas
observador.description: Partido propõe dedução de 1.200 euros por cada terceiro filho e seguintes, de forma gradual até 2028. Medida custaria 20 milhões por ano ao Estado.

observador.title: Mais de 8 anos de prisão por agredir e violar companheira
observador.description: O arguido, de 35 anos, vivia com a vítima há cerca de cinco meses em Campo Maior. Para além da pena de prisão, foi condenado a pagar 10 mil euros em indemnização.

observador.title: Irão. NATO diz que 500 aeronaves dos EUA saíram de Itália
observador.description: Mark Rutte rejeitou a narrativa de Trump de que aliados europeus dos EUA não prestaram ajuda. "Estamos a falar de entre 4.000 e 5.000 missões de voo", em toda a Europa. Só 500 descolaram de Itália.

observador.title: Incêndios: ministro diz que Forças Armadas estão preparadas
observador.description: Dois C-130 entram ao serviço em 2027 e dois Canadair chegam em 2029 e 2030. Nuno Melo anunciou as novidades em Figueiró dos Vinhos, onde foi distinguido com a Medalha de Honra.

spiegel.title: Favorit für die Starmer-Nachfolge in Großbritannien: Der freche Junge aus Manchester
spiegel.description: Keir Starmers instinktlose Politik hat die Labour-Partei in eine schwere Krise geführt. Sein möglicher Nachfolger Andy Burnham hat gezeigt, dass er Nigel Farages rechtspopulistische Partei Reform UK schlagen kann. Wer ist der Mann?

spiegel.title: Streit zwischen Polen und der Ukraine: »Chaos, multipliziert mit Hysterie«
spiegel.description: Präsident Selenskyj reist nicht zu einer Ukrainekonferenz nach Danzig, die Beziehung zu Polen ist auf einem Tiefpunkt. Der ukrainische Historiker Jaroslaw Hryzak warnt, der Streit gefährde den europäischen Erweiterungsprozess.

spiegel.title: Martin Reichardt: AfD-Politiker soll Hitlergruß gezeigt haben
spiegel.description: Auf einem Foto streckt Martin Reichardt einen Arm nach oben. Union und Grüne fordern seinen Rücktritt. Der sachsen-anhaltische AfD-Chef weist Hitlergruß-Vorwürfe zurück.

spiegel.title: Kriegsverbrecher-Tribunal in Den Haag: Wohin mit den Beweisen für ein Jahrhundertverbrechen?
spiegel.description: Rund 24 Jahre lang verfolgte ein Uno-Strafgericht Kriegsverbrechen in den Ländern des ehemaligen Jugoslawiens. Davon zeugen kilometerweise Akten, Videos und andere Beweise. Nun wollen die Niederlande das Archiv offenbar loswerden.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Deutsche Bahn, Friedrich Merz, Rente, Klima, Elon Musk, SpaceX
spiegel.description: Nach einem Ausfall wegen Funkstille rollen die Züge wieder. Merz muss sich fragen lassen, ob er die Rente rettet, aber das Klima schrottet. Und Elon Musk ist nur noch Milliardär. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochabend.

spiegel.title: Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg: Besuch der Plaza soll bald Eintritt kosten
spiegel.description: Wer die Aussichtsplattform der Hamburger Elbphilharmonie kostenfrei betreten möchte, hat noch etwas mehr als drei Monate Zeit. Danach will die Stadt 3 bis 5 Euro für den Zutritt zu ihrem größten Balkon kassieren.

spiegel.title: Hitze-News: Spanien misst höchste Juni-Temperaturen seit mehr als 70 Jahren
spiegel.description: In Spanien erreicht die Hitzewelle ihren Höhepunkt. Der Flughafen Hannover muss die Landebahn wässern. Und: Die Hitzeprognose für Deutschland. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: Michelle und Barack Obama schwärmen von ihrer Beziehung
spiegel.description: In einem gemeinsamen Interview klingen der frühere US-Präsident und die einstige First Lady nicht nach Krise. Ist das die Magie ihrer Heimatstadt Chicago?

spiegel.title: Zweibrücken: Angeklagter bittet Familie des getöteten Bahn-Mitarbeiters um Vergebung
spiegel.description: Ioanni V. soll im Februar brutal auf den Zugbegleiter Serkan Ç. eingeschlagen haben, der zweifache Vater starb. Zum Prozessauftakt lässt der Angeklagte eine Erklärung verlesen, in der er die Tat einen »Moment blinder Wut« nennt.

spiegel.title: Luigi Pantisanos Äußerungen: Friedrich Merz lehnt Zusammenarbeit mit der Linkspartei erneut ab
spiegel.description: Linkenchef Pantisano hat sich für seinen Faschisten-Vergleich bei der CDU entschuldigt. Merz sieht trotzdem keine Zukunft für eine Zusammenarbeit der beiden Parteien.

spiegel.title: Rente: Manuela Schwesig setzt auf riskante Abgrenzung zur Koalition
spiegel.description: Manuela Schwesig grenzt sich deutlich von der schwarz-roten Koalition ab, zuletzt beim Thema Rente. Dahinter steht eine riskante Strategie. Aber die Ministerpräsidentin könnte damit Erfolg haben.

spiegel.title: Operation Endgame: Microsoft und BKA legen Hunderte Schadsoftware-Server lahm
spiegel.description: In einer international koordinierten Aktion haben Ermittler kriminellen Akteuren einen schweren Schlag versetzt. Um einige der meistgenutzten Schadprogramme weltweit zu stoppen, kam auch KI zum Einsatz.

spiegel.title: Renningen, Baden-Württemberg: Polizei ermittelt nach Fund von Babyleiche gegen Mutter
spiegel.description: Überraschende Wende nach dem Fund eines toten Säuglings in Renningen: Die Mutter könnte den Ermittlern zufolge eine Entführung nur vorgetäuscht haben.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Welche Gruppendritten kommen weiter? Der SPIEGEL-Check
spiegel.description: Wer kommt weiter, wer scheidet aus? Erstmals ziehen bei einer Fußball-WM die acht besten Gruppendritten in die K.-o.-Phase ein. Im Check zeigt sich: Es wird verdammt eng – und nicht jedes Team sollte auf Sieg spielen.

spiegel.title: Esa-Weltraumteleskop »Euclid« zeigt helles Zentrum der Milchstraße
spiegel.description: Die Aufnahme des Weltraumteleskops »Euclid« ist eine der detailliertesten vom inneren Bereich unserer Galaxie. Das Bild soll helfen, die Existenz von Planeten in fremden Sonnensystemen zu bestätigen.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Was der bundesweite Ausfall über Verwundbarkeit deutscher Infrastruktur verrät – Meinung
spiegel.description: Der bundesweite Ausfall des Bahnverkehrs hat wieder einmal gezeigt, wie anfällig die Infrastruktur in Deutschland ist. Das Chaos sollte endlich ein Weckruf für die deutsche Investitionspolitik sein.

spiegel.title: FDP: Öffnung nach rechts? Kritik an Hagens Gespräch mit der »Jungen Freiheit«
spiegel.description: Der neue FDP-Generalsekretär Martin Hagen gibt der »Jungen Freiheit« ein Interview – und sorgt damit in seiner Partei für Aufregung. Dabei dürfte sich kaum ein Liberaler über die Aktion wundern.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

letemps.title: Après l’AVS et le rail, l’armée veut aussi sa part de la TVA
letemps.description:
Face aux menaces grandissantes, comment financer le réarmement de la Suisse? Le Conseil fédéral a choisi: une hausse de la TVA de 0,5 point. Défendue par Martin Pfister, chef du Département de la défense, la mesure pourrait rapporter 24 milliards de francs en douze ans, mais elle peine pour l’heure à convaincre

letemps.title: La gauche lausannoise exige plus de fermeté pour les employés de la Ville condamnés pénalement

phys-org.title: Automated system detects early signs of nanomaterials toxicity
phys-org.description: Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science has developed a toxicity assessment system that automatically measures and analyzes the heart rate of Daphnia magna. Capable of processing heart rate data from approximately 150 individuals per hour, the system can assess the toxic effects of pollutants at low concentrations more sensitively than conventional methods that rely on average values from a small number of specimens. The technology is expected to help detect early warning signs of haza

phys-org.title: Artificial DNA tiles could deliver drugs and monitor neurons non-disruptively
phys-org.description: Living cells constantly exchange ions (i.e., charged particles) via the thin barrier that surrounds their interior, known as the outer membrane. Neuroscientists and medical researchers have long been trying to devise effective methods to measure this exchange of ions, which is known to be associated with communication between neurons and various other crucial physiological processes.

phys-org.title: New giant wormlion fly species identified on the southern slopes of the Himalayas
phys-org.description: An enigmatic new species of wormlion fly, whose larvae construct clever pitfall traps to capture prey, has been revealed in a study led by researchers at Dali University in China.

phys-org.description: People living in Germany have more confidence in themselves today than 20 years ago. They have more faith in their ability to influence their own lives and key life events. This has now been shown in a long-term study conducted by Dr. Theresa M. Entringer from the University of Greifswald and colleagues from Berlin and the U.S., based on the Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP). Data from more than 42,000 individuals were analyzed for this purpose. The examination period spanned more than two decades; th

phys-org.title: Why female guppies prefer rare males and how this might shape evolution
phys-org.description: When it comes to choosing a partner, some species prefer males that stand out from the crowd. Evolutionary biologists call the resulting process negative frequency-dependent selection. It means that a male has a huge mating advantage when his appearance is rare but loses that advantage if his look becomes too common. This constant balancing act may be one important reason for the variety in nature.

phys-org.title: Teaching with and about GenAI in classrooms
phys-org.description: It is important that teachers and students are aware of and understand the major shortcomings of technology, state Norwegian researchers who have studied the use of AI in the classroom.

phys-org.title: Asteroid zooming past Earth on Saturday visible to stargazers
phys-org.description: A large asteroid that will zoom harmlessly past Earth on Saturday will be visible to stargazers using a small telescope or large binoculars, the European Space Agency announced Wednesday.

phys-org.title: By making key signaling molecules called β-arrestins into druggable targets, scientists crack long-standing challenge
phys-org.description: To function normally, nearly every cell in the human body relies on G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) to receive and send signals. That's why GPCRs are targeted by roughly one-third of all FDA-approved drugs.

phys-org.title: Surprising diversity found among Europe's last Neanderthals
phys-org.description: A new study published in Nature provides the most detailed picture to date of Neanderthal diversity in Western Europe shortly before their extinction.

phys-org.title: First complete map of world's seagrass offers warnings and hope for conservation
phys-org.description: It's time we gave seagrass the credit it's due. This hero of a plant protects coastlines, stores vast amounts of carbon and supports ecosystems that people and wildlife depend on. But we don't often hear about it when it comes to ocean conservation. That's partly because we knew so little about it—until now.

phys-org.title: Turning low-value diamond dust into high-performance quantum materials
phys-org.description: Diamonds have long been coveted for their beauty. Their dazzling color and clarity make them perfect candidates for luxury jewelry. However, it's their other unique characteristics, including their hardness, thermal conductivity and chemical resistance, that make diamonds suitable for various applications in industry and advanced technologies.

phys-org.title: Quantum squeezing sidesteps the limits on mechanical transducers
phys-org.description: From detecting the ripples of colliding black holes to imaging individual chemical bonds, mechanical transducers have repeatedly transformed our understanding of the universe. So far, however, the sensitivity of these devices has been intrinsically limited by the laws of quantum mechanics itself.

phys-org.title: Axolotl-inspired skin matrix may help heal wounds with less scarring
phys-org.description: Researchers in Taiwan have developed a cell-free extracellular matrix material from axolotl skin that helped mouse burn wounds close faster and show signs of reduced fibrotic scarring. The findings suggest that one of nature's most remarkable regenerators may inspire future strategies for burns, chronic wounds and surgical injuries, but the approach is not yet a treatment for human wounds.

phys-org.title: Scientists catch classical space-time crystals moving like Majorana quasiparticles
phys-org.description: A research team from Hiroshima University, the University of Colorado, and other collaborators have demonstrated that space-time crystals—exotic structures that, under external drive, loop endlessly through both space and time—can be created using everyday liquid-crystal materials.

phys-org.title: Voluntary corporate climate goals are viewed favorably by investors, researchers discover
phys-org.description: As companies face increasing pressure to address climate change, many are choosing to publicly announce voluntary carbon-elimination goals.

phys-org.title: Sugar-coated nanoparticles show promise for treating most aggressive form of brain cancer
phys-org.description: Researchers at Oregon State University have potentially found a new way to treat the most aggressive form of brain cancer, glioblastoma, whose two-year survival rate is less than 30%.

phys-org.title: Five years of aerosol remote sensing in Mindelo—a milestone in atmospheric research in the Atlantic
phys-org.description: For five years now, a distinctive green laser beam has been shining at night up to 30 kilometers (19 miles) above the harbor of the island's capital. It forms part of a high-energy lidar with which the Leibniz Institute for Atmospheric Research (TROPOS) operates continuous aerosol and cloud measurements at the Ocean Science Center Mindelo (OSCM).

phys-org.title: From virtue to vice: How the morality of popular music lyrics has changed since the 1960s
phys-org.description: Popular music may be reflecting a growing culture of vices, according to new research from the Center for Digital Music at Queen Mary University of London. The analysis of musical evolution found that song lyrics have become increasingly negative over the past six decades, with declining references to moral virtues. This could provide an important indicator of a cultural shift in society.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.
